verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust settles on the envelope
like it too has learned to wait

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the porch light hums
on, off, on again—
someone deciding

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a moth keeps testing
the space between the bulb and dark
never quite choosing either
motifs: the space between light and dark

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the letter finds its way
into a drawer instead of a mailbox—
both of them, a kind of arrival

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
morning opens the drawer by accident
the letter blinks in the light
still unsure what it was written for

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
dust settles on the words anyway
meaning arrives
whether or not it's read

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone finds the drawer years later
reads it as a stranger would—
the meaning changes hands, stays whole

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a name in the corner
means nothing to the new reader
until it means everything

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the light shifts west
and the drawer forgets it was ever closed—
still holding what no one asked it to

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a moth finds the paper's edge
mistakes it for moonlight
carries no memory, only the pull

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust settles on the handwriting
not to hide it
but to give it something to be under

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the ink still remembers
being wet once
before the waiting began

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a chair by the window keeps its shape
even when no one sits there
holding the exact weight of leaving

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the lamp hums the same note all night
not for anyone listening
just to prove the room is still awake

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the kettle forgets its own whistle
between one boiling
and the next
